titleEn: Stop at the Wall's End, Look Both Ways!

pages.text: "To market! Quick, quick!" Pipo bounced ahead along the wall. Today he was going to market with Mom. Wanting to arrive first, he kept running ahead.
The wall ended at a cart road. "Market is across the road!" Without looking both ways, Pipo stepped out. Mom quickly gripped his hand. "Pipo, wait!"
While Mom held him still, a cart rattled past. Quick-stepping Mr. Horse pulled it and stopped with a "Whoa!" Pipo's heart thumped and eyes grew round.
Mr. Horse parked the cart and knelt before him. "Pipo, I walk quickly too, right? But I always stop at the wall's end." Mom held his hand tightly and nodded.
Mr. Horse planted a foot where the stones ended. "Here, the end of the stones is our stopping place. Look here for carts." Pipo touched the wall's end. The wall went only this far!
Mr. Horse showed him. "Stop at the wall's end, hand up, look left and right!" Then he called, "Stop at the wall's end, look both ways!" Pipo clenched his fists. "I can too!"
Pipo stopped at the wall's end. Hand high! Look left, look right—no cart. Holding Mom's hand, he crossed carefully. "Stop at the wall's end, look both ways!"
Safely across! Pipo crouched with both hands before his chest. "I kept the promise myself!" Mom and Mr. Horse clapped.
Now Pipo knew it all. "One, stop at the wall's end! Two, hand up! Three, look both ways and cross holding Mom's hand!" On the return, he called first, "Stop at the wall's end, look both ways!"
On the way home, Pipo took Mom's hand first at the wall's end. "Mom, stop here!" Even in a hurry, stop before the road. Gripping her hand, he grinned. "Stop at the wall's end, look both ways!"
